description: Baude's Settings dialog: a General page of settings, a Subscriptions page (the Claude and Codex accounts of the host picked beside New session), a Dependencies page (what that host and the app need, each there or not) and a Telemetry page (what that host keeps: its turns' tokens, its machine, its chats' activity, line profiles), each applied as it is changed and kept in settings.json (shared with Record, which has its own Settings dialog with the same rows). Title "Settings".
opens: key Cmd+, (macOS) / Ctrl+, (elsewhere); the key again while it is open leaves it

parts.name: Subscriptions page
parts.shows: The dialog's second page, after General (the existing rows): the Claude and Codex accounts of the host picked beside New session. Described in Subscriptions.dialog.json.

decisions.said: Baude needs to be able to support running claude with different subscriptions (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Settings has the Subscriptions page after General, switched to by the dialog's page switcher (on a narrow screen, the phone's included, the bar at its foot)

decisions.said: There needs to be a way of seeing claude sub usage in the app
decisions.rule: Subscription usage is on that page in every app

parts.name: Dependencies page
parts.shows: The dialog's third page, after Subscriptions: what the host picked beside New session needs for its features and whether it's there, then the app's own. Described in Dependencies.dialog.json.

decisions.said: Think about guidance for installing what Baude depends on (claude, codex, vte3, kubectl, docker) and how Baude behaves when they aren't there (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Settings has a Dependencies page after Subscriptions, switched to by the dialog's page switcher (the phone's bar at its foot)

parts.name: Telemetry page
parts.shows: The dialog's fourth page, after Dependencies: what the host picked beside New session keeps of its turns, its machine, its chats' activity and its line profiles. Described in Telemetry.dialog.json.

decisions.said: Baude needs telemetry: screen time per place in the UI, and some sign of which features are used (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Settings has a Telemetry page after Dependencies, switched to by the dialog's page switcher (the phone's bar at its foot)

parts.name: Meta group
parts.shows: The first group, Meta's settings (Intelligence, Provider, Effort, Run commands, Code mode), the same rows Meta's own page has. Described in MetaSettings.dialog.json.

parts.name: General group (no title)
parts.shows: One group of seven rows, in this order.

parts.name: Full-width text
parts.shows: A row titled "Full-width text" with a switch at the right, no subtitle. The switch is the same setting as the ☰ menu's "Full-width text" item, so the two always agree. On: the chat's text column runs the full width of the window; off: held to a readable column.

actions.by: click anywhere on the row or the switch
actions.does: toggles full-width text at once in the open chat and keeps it

decisions.said: For new installations full-width text should be the default.
decisions.rule: Every app starts a fresh installation with Full-width text on.

parts.name: Code Font
parts.shows: A row titled "Code Font" with a drop-down of the code fonts this machine has, the current one selected. When the picked font is not the one running now, the row's subtitle reads "<font> from Baude's next start" and a Restart button shows at the right of the row; when the pick is the running font there is no subtitle and no button.

actions.does: keeps it in settings.json; it takes effect at the next start (fonts are set up before the app starts); the subtitle and Restart button appear
closes Settings, then restarts Baude as ☰ → Restart Baude does

parts.name: Accent Colour
parts.shows: A row titled "Accent Colour" with a drop-down. Its first entry is "System" (the platform's own accent), then libadwaita's accents: Blue, Teal, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red, Pink, Purple, Slate. Each entry, in the list and in the closed drop-down, is a 12 px round dot of that colour then the name (System's dot is the colour the system accent is now, or the theme's accent while Settings → Theme has one that sets it).

phone.does: applies it in the app at once and keeps it; System clears the choice. The launcher icon keeps Baude's colours, and on Android 13 and later its monochrome layer follows the system's palette when the launcher's themed icons are on
phone.why: Android can't recolour an app's launcher icon as it runs; swapping launcher aliases per accent drops the icon from the home screen on common launchers

actions.does: applies it in every open Baude and Record window at once and keeps it; System clears the choice. Baude's and Record's logos take it too: the logo's tile colour (schema/icons/apps) becomes the accent's, in the macOS Dock tile, the windows' icon elsewhere, and the launcher if the app is in the platform's list of apps; with System they keep their own colours

decisions.said: Let me change Baude's accent colour in Settings; I want it orange (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Settings has Accent Colour (System, or a named accent such as Orange), one setting shared by the apps, applied in every open window at once.

decisions.said: Asked that Meta changing the theme go the same route as a click and get the same animation.
decisions.rule: Every app changes the accent the same way whoever changes it (picked in Settings or set by Meta): the window cross-fades into the new accent over 200 ms.

decisions.said: The Baude icon should take the selected accent on platforms that allow it (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app whose platform lets it recolour its icon draws its logo in the accent picked (the Dock tile, the windows' icon, the launcher entry); with System it keeps its own colours

parts.name: Theme
parts.shows: A row titled "Theme" with a drop-down: "Default" (Baude's own look) first, then the themes this machine's host keeps (its themes request), by name. Before the host answers it lists Default and the theme picked. A theme is a folder on its host, themes/<name>/ in its data folder, of theme.css (GTK CSS, drawn over all of the desktop apps' own, at USER priority) and tokens.json (colours over schema/tokens', light and dark: a resolver document as baude.resolver.json is, setting libadwaita's and baude's colours only); the host works out each colour it makes (Theme.json), and every app draws those. A theme's accent is drawn only while Accent Colour is System; an accent picked there is drawn over it everywhere (the window, the logo, the phone). Each time a theme is drawn it's tried on a probe first (a label and a button in a window no one sees, drawn by hand: their text's colour and size, and how it stands out from what's under it); if the text can't be seen, has no size or can't be told from its background, Default is drawn for this run and a toast in each window says so: "Couldn't use the theme <name>: <why>. Showing Default." Started with BAUDE_NO_THEME=1 (or an app's --no-theme), an app draws Default whatever is picked, till a theme is picked again.

actions.does: draws it in every Baude, Record, Emission and Multiplex window here at once (and the other apps here, which follow the setting) and keeps it in settings.json (theme; Default clears it); the theme's files changing on disk (Meta's create_theme) are drawn again as they change

draws it in the app at once and keeps it, with its colours as the host gave them, so it draws from the next start before the host is reached; the theme picked is taken again whenever the host lists it

actions.by: a theme whose probe's text can't be read (picked, previewed, or its files changed)
actions.does: draws Default for this run instead, and says why in a toast in each window here

decisions.said: Look at what Claude Mods does for the Claude app's themes: give Baude a way, from the inside, for Meta to create, install and preview themes in Settings, as generic as it can be while staying fast (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Settings has a Theme row after Accent Colour: Default, then the themes of a host (the desktop's own machine's; the phone's, the host picked beside New session). A theme is its host's, worked out there for every app alike, so one theme draws the same colours on every app, light and dark

decisions.said: A theme could make every app unreadable (its text transparent, or everything at opacity 0) with no way back from inside the apps (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app tries a theme on a probe before keeping it drawn, and draws Default, saying why, when the probe's text can't be read; every app can be started in Default whatever theme is picked (BAUDE_NO_THEME=1, --no-theme)

decisions.said: Picking an Accent Colour did nothing while a theme set its own accent (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: A theme's accent is drawn only while Accent Colour is System; an accent picked is drawn over it in every app (the window, the logo, the phone), and System's dot shows the theme's accent while it sets one

parts.name: Appearance
parts.shows: A row titled "Appearance" with a drop-down at its end showing the current choice: Follow System (the default), Light or Dark. The phone's own: the desktop follows the platform.

actions.does: applies it to the whole app at once and keeps it

parts.name: Show in launcher

decisions.said: The added to application menu path shouldn't go into the chat; it should be a toast
decisions.rule: Every app says what turning this on or off did in a toast, never as a note in the chat

decisions.said: if "Add apps in application register (on MAcos the command+search pane, on androdid the app list and such), we should make sure that all of: Record, Baude, Emission, Multiplex are all visible and vice versa for when it is removed
decisions.rule: Every app's Show in Applications setting adds Baude, Record, Emission and Multiplex to the platform's list of apps together and takes all four out together; it's one setting shared by every app

parts.shows: A row titled "Show in application menu" on Linux or "Show in Applications" on macOS, with a switch and no subtitle. One setting for Baude, Record, Emission and Multiplex together, the same as Record's Settings row and every app's --install / --uninstall: on when all four are in the platform's list of apps, read again each time Settings opens. Turning it on also writes the commands in ~/.local/bin (baude, record, emission, multiplex, baude-headless, baude-oneshot), which the launchers start; turning it off leaves them, as other machines reach this one's host process through ~/.local/bin/baude-headless.

phone.why: Adding the app to the freedesktop application menu or the macOS Applications list has no phone equivalent (the phone's app is installed and updated as its own build)

actions.does: adds Baude, Record, Emission and Multiplex to (a .desktop file and icon each, or a macOS app bundle each in ~/Applications, which Spotlight finds; Baude's and Record's logos in the accent picked) or removes all four from the platform's list of apps; a note in the chat says what was done ("added to <where>: <path>", "removed from <where>"), or the error; the switch ends up showing the real state

parts.name: Auto restart on update
parts.shows: A switch row titled "Auto restart on update". Subtitle "From <upstream> every <N>s, restarting once idle" (upstream is the branch the checkout follows, N the check interval in seconds). With no upstream (not a git checkout following a branch) the subtitle is "Not a git checkout following a branch: nothing to update from" and the switch is greyed and off. Off by default: an update runs code from the upstream. One setting shared by Baude and Record; follows a change made in the other app.

phone.does: Update on metered connections (the phone's own updater)
phone.why: The phone installs builds, not a git checkout

actions.does: turns the automatic fetch, fast-forward and restart-once-idle on or off, and keeps it

parts.name: Update on metered connections
parts.shows: A switch row titled "Update on metered connections", subtitle "Whether to download when only 5G/4G is available". Off by default: a newer build then waits for Update on a metered network.

actions.does: keeps it; turning it on looks for a newer build at once

parts.name: Notifications
parts.shows: A switch row titled "Notifications", subtitle "When a reply finishes, or asks you something, while you're elsewhere". On unless turned off. Shared by Baude and Record.

actions.does: turns desktop notifications on or off and keeps it

parts.name: Version
parts.shows: An information row (no switch, no link, nothing to click). Title "Version <short hash>" (the commit this running process's code is); subtitle the date and time that commit was made, like "21 November 2026, 09:14". If the code is not in a git checkout: title "Version unknown", subtitle "Not a git checkout". It does NOT lead to the changelog: the changelog is only reached from ☰ → Changelog (and from the commit links in ☰ → Mesh, and under Meta's reply).

parts.name: Size group
parts.shows: A group titled "Size" with three numeric stepper rows (a number with - and + buttons, one decimal digit, steps of 0.1), 1.0 the usual.

parts.name: Text Scale
parts.shows: Row "Text Scale", range 0.7 to 2.0, the saved value (default 1.0). Scales all text in every open window of Baude and Record.

actions.does: applies the text size at once in every window and keeps it; follows the other app changing it

parts.name: Icon Scale
parts.shows: Row "Icon Scale", range 0.7 to 2.0 (default 1.0). Scales icons (16 px at 1.0) in every window.

actions.does: applies the icon size at once in every window and keeps it

parts.name: Global Scale
parts.shows: Row "Global Scale", range 0.6 to 2.5, this window's current chat zoom default (what Cmd+0 / Ctrl+0 goes back to).

actions.does: sets the zoom the chat returns to on the reset-zoom key, and keeps it as zoom_default

parts.name: Send Feedback row
parts.shows: A last group of one row, a button row titled "Send Feedback…" with a go-next chevron at its end.

actions.does: closes Settings first (the captures are of the window, not of the dialog over it), then opens the Send Feedback dialog (SendFeedback.dialog.json)

states.name: no upstream
states.shows: Auto restart row greyed, off, with the "Not a git checkout…" subtitle

states.name: code font changed, not yet running
states.shows: Code Font row has the "from Baude's next start" subtitle and a Restart button

states.name: not a git checkout
states.shows: Version row says "Version unknown" / "Not a git checkout"

states.name: setting changed by the other app
states.shows: The row for any shared setting (accent, code font, notifications, auto restart, scales) updates to the new value without running its own handler

decisions.said: Asked that settings shared by the apps (accent, font, auto update, text/global/icon scale, Meta's model) spread across the apps on the same host, not across the mesh.
decisions.rule: Every app on a machine shares its common settings (accent, code font, auto restart on update, text, icon and global scale, Meta's model and settings) and follows a change made in another at once; window zoom (Ctrl +/-/0) stays each window's, and nothing is shared across the mesh.
